classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish square and rectangular tiles using the taught key, count each type, and write their total as separate x² and x terms.

content.prompt: Write an expression for the total area.

spec.description: Two slightly tilted square tiles in a vertical pair on the left; two rectangular tiles in a vertical pair immediately to their right; a third rectangle farther right between them.
spec.mathematics: Each square represents area x² and each rectangle represents area x, as defined on page 14. No numerical dimensions are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Tile geometry is permanent; the total expression appears only in answers.

answer.worked: Two $x^2$ tiles and three $x$ tiles give $2x^2+3x$.

spec.description: Two square tiles in the upper row; a third square centred below them between two vertical rectangular tiles. Tiles remain separate and slightly tilted.
spec.mathematics: The square and rectangle areas are x² and x respectively.
spec.answerVisibility: Tile geometry is permanent; the total expression appears only in answers.

answer.worked: Three $x^2$ tiles and two $x$ tiles give $3x^2+2x$.

spec.description: Three square tiles in the upper row. The lower row contains four vertical rectangles, one square and a fifth rectangle, in that order.
spec.mathematics: Four x² tiles and five x tiles; no printed dimensions or internal labels.
spec.answerVisibility: Tile geometry is permanent; the total expression appears only in answers.

answer.worked: Four $x^2$ tiles and five $x$ tiles give $4x^2+5x$.
